newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SCHIPHOL FREIGHT CHARGES SYSTEM TO BE DROPPED.
newsitem.headline: SCHIPHOL FREIGHT CHARGES SYSTEM TO BE DROPPED.

text.p: A unique system of handling charges paid by air freight shippers at Schiphol airport is to be phased out by January 1 next year, the Air Transport Association of the Netherlands (ATAN) said in a statement.
The trade body, which represents Netherlands-based air cargo carriers, said a compromise has been reached between its members and the Dutch association of air freight handling firms, NVVL.

The charges, known as zendingskosten, had been the focus of an independent study commissed to resolve a controversial debate about handling charges which had split the shipping, airline, freight forwarding and cargo handling sectors.
ATAN said that over the first six months of this year, all parties concerned will implement a new system, which aims to cut the charges applied by around 50 percent.

The charges, estimated to cost shippers 5-8 million guilders a year, have traditionally been levied at the Netherlands' leading airport by cargo handlers and forwarders for receiving air freight as it arrives at the airport for onward despatch.

ATAN said the aim is to gradually reduce the costs in the first part of this year and reduce them still further in the second half of 1997 in anticipation of scrapping the charge from January 1 next year.
The zendingskosten system has no equivalent at other European airports, and is perceived by Dutch shippers, and their trade organisation EVO, to be unfair.

The charges evolved in the days when air freight needed to be prepared for carriage. Dutch shippers argue that they have no place today when cargo arrives ready for shipment. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
